name: Quan Chen
intro: I am an undergraduate at Peking University, pursuing a dual degree in Mathematics and Computer Science. I expect to graduate in June 2027.
My research focuses on large language models, including agentic reasoning, reinforcement learning and post-training, safety alignment, and decoding for language diffusion models.
Outside research, I share course notes and small projects on my blog, and enjoy listening to JJ Lin.

news.text: I joined Optiver as a quantitative trader intern.
We open-sourced SearchSwarm, a multi-agent framework for long-horizon deep research.
I joined the BaiLing Foundation Model Team at Ant Group as an LLM post-training research intern.
1 paper accepted by ICML 2025 Workshop on Models of Human Feedback for AI Alignment.

publications.title: SearchSwarm: Towards Delegation Intelligence in Agentic LLMs for Long-Horizon Deep Research
publications.description: A multi-agent framework that uses sub-agents for active context management in long-horizon deep research, with supervised fine-tuning data for learning delegation.

publications.title: Decoding Large Language Diffusion Models with Foreseeing Movement
publications.description: A search-based decoding method that combines local and global information for discrete optimization, with an accelerated variant that concentrates search on selected decoding steps.

publications.title: Advancing LLM Safe Alignment with Safety Representation Ranking
publications.venue: ICML 2025 Workshop: Models of Human Feedback for AI Alignment.
publications.description: A safety-alignment method that ranks candidate responses using intermediate Transformer representations and a lightweight similarity scorer.

projects.title: SearchSwarm
projects.description: An open-source multi-agent framework for long-horizon deep research. Trains research agents to delegate subtasks and use compact, evidence-grounded reports for active context management.

projects.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Chinese Official Mahjong
projects.description: Built an agent trained through behavior cloning and self-play PPO, with an asymmetric actor-critic model and IMPALA-style asynchronous training. Ranked 5th out of 28 teams in the final round of the Botzone competition.
projects.label: Reinforcement learning · Self-play · Multi-process training
